explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/427, which quotes Shiu [Sh00]: 'for any l ≥ 1 and (a,q) = 1 there exist infinitely many l-tuples of consecutive primes p_m, …, p_{m+l−1} all of which are congruent to a modulo q.' ShiuTheorem states: for all k ≥ 1, q ≥ 1 and a coprime to q, the set of m such that every prime Nat.nth Nat.Prime i with i ∈ [m, m+k) is ≡ a (mod q) is infinite. Consecutive indices give consecutive primes; the 0-based indexing is immaterial for an 'infinitely many' statement. Faithful.
